original_question:
Consider the ionization-coupled variants of the focusing cubic NLS used for laser filamentation, namely the fixed-frame system

 i(partial_t + c_g partial_z)u + epsilon(Delta_perp + alpha_1 partial_z^2)u + epsilon(|u|^2 - rho)u = -i epsilon c(alpha_4 |u|^{2K-2}u + alpha_5 rho u),
 partial_t rho = epsilon alpha_4 |u|^{2K} + epsilon alpha_5 rho |u|^2,

and the moving-frame version

 i partial_tau v + (Delta_perp + alpha_1 partial_z^2)v + (|v|^2 - rho_tilde)v = -i c(alpha_4 |v|^{2K-2}v + alpha_5 rho_tilde v),
 -c_g partial_z rho_tilde = epsilon alpha_4 |v|^{2K} + epsilon alpha_5 rho_tilde |v|^2,

where the paper prescribes the boundary condition lim_{z -> +infinity} (nabla_perp)^l rho_tilde(tau, X_perp, z) = 0 for all l >= 0. Can one prove that solutions of these ionization models are global in dimensions 2 and 3, so that ionization really prevents finite-time collapse?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1.2, Open Problem 3: prove that the solutions to equations (54) and (55) are global in dimensions 2 and 3.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct ionization-coupled models, reproduces the fixed-frame and moving-frame systems corresponding to (54) and (55), includes the paper’s boundary condition at z -> +infinity for ρ̃, and asks exactly the same qualitative question as the paper: whether ionization prevents finite-time breakdown by forcing global existence in dimensions 2 and 3.
missing_details: The paper’s exact target is Open Problem 3 in Section 4.1.2, not a broader question about all ionization-modified filamentation models.
The scope is the simplest scalar setting obtained from the general model by taking P2 = I, α2 = 0, α3 = 0, and f = 0; your draft leaves these restrictions implicit.

The dimension/GVD regime is part of the statement: d = 2 corresponds to no GVD (α1 = 0) and d = 3 corresponds to anomalous GVD (α1 = 1); the paper is not posing this open problem for arbitrary α1 or for normal GVD.

Equation (55) is only an approximation of the transformed fixed-frame system: after the change of variables ρ(t, X⊥, z) = ρ̃(εt, X⊥, z - c_g t), the paper drops the ε∂τρ̃ term. So (54) and (55) are not presented as exactly equivalent formulations.
The ambient variables/operators should be made explicit: x = (X⊥, z) ∈ R^d with X⊥ ∈ R^(d-1), Δ⊥ is the transverse Laplacian, and c_g = c_g e_z.
The parameter restrictions should be stated explicitly: α4, α5 ≥ 0, c > 0, and K > 0 (physically, the number of photons needed for photo-ionization).

To make 'solutions are global' precise, the natural local regularity classes discussed just before the open problem should be named: for (54), local existence is derived in H^N × H^N for N > d/2; for (55), in the mixed space 𝓗^N × 𝓗^N for N > d, where 𝓗^N = {f : Σ_{j=0}^N ||∇^j f||_(L^2_{X⊥}L^∞_z) < ∞}.
Nonnegativity of the electron density is part of the nearby setup: ρ is an electron density, and for (55) the boundary condition at +infinity is chosen precisely so that ρ̃ ≥ 0.
refined_question: For the scalar ionization models considered in Section 4.1.2—namely, in the regime of no or anomalous GVD, with α1 = 0 when d = 2 and α1 = 1 when d = 3, and with the remaining parameters fixed to P2 = I, α2 = 0, α3 = 0, and f = 0—let x = (X⊥, z) ∈ R^d, X⊥ ∈ R^(d-1), Δ⊥ denote the transverse Laplacian, c_g = c_g e_z, and assume α4, α5 ≥ 0, c > 0, K > 0. For the fixed-frame system i(∂t + c_g∂z)u + ε(Δ⊥ + α1∂z^2)u + ε(|u|^2 - ρ)u = -iεc(α4|u|^(2K-2)u + α5ρu), ∂tρ = εα4|u|^(2K) + εα5ρ|u|^2, and for its moving-frame approximation i∂τv + (Δ⊥ + α1∂z^2)v + (|v|^2 - ρ̃)v = -ic(α4|v|^(2K-2)v + α5ρ̃v), -c_g∂zρ̃ = εα4|v|^(2K) + εα5ρ̃|v|^2, supplemented with the boundary condition lim_{z→+∞}(∇⊥)^l ρ̃(τ, X⊥, z) = 0 for every l ≥ 0, prove that the corresponding local solutions in the natural classes used in Section 4.1.2 extend globally forward in time in dimensions d = 2 and d = 3; equivalently, show that these ionization terms prevent finite-time breakdown for the two specific models (54) and (55).
justification: This draft is targeting Open Problem 3 in Section 4.1.2. The paper first introduces the ionization systems in the Introduction as equations (4) and (5), explains that the moving-frame model is obtained after a change of variables and an approximation in the ρ-equation, and then returns to them in Section 4.1.2 as equations (54) and (55) with boundary condition (56). Immediately before Open Problem 3, the authors discuss local well-posedness for these systems, observe that the L^2 norm is dissipated but that the energy is neither conserved nor monotone, and then formulate exactly the question your draft is aiming at: whether taking ionization into account prevents finite-time breakdown in dimensions 2 and 3. Your draft is therefore very close, but it needs the paper’s scope restrictions (simplest scalar case, no/anomalous GVD only), the status of (55) as an approximation rather than an exact reformulation, and the natural local-well-posedness setting to become fully stand-alone and paper-faithful.
